An **interpretation / hypothesis-generation** report (not a predictive
leaderboard — at n=9 a deployable predictor isn't the goal). Ordered categories
(Green < Ripe < Overripe); samples are independent fruit, so cross-validation is
leave-one-out and serves as a **guardrail**, not a performance claim. Multi-omics
integration uses **R mixOmics DIABLO** (the reference implementation); reductions
use PCA/NMF (sklearn). See `docs/ASSUMPTIONS_AND_CHOICES.md`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path
HERE = Path.cwd()
for cand in (HERE, HERE / "examples" / "banana_report"):
    if (cand / "analysis.py").exists():
        sys.path.insert(0, str(cand)); break
import analysis
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Markdown
res = analysis.run_banana_analysis()
```

# Part 1 — Multi-omics integration (DIABLO, R mixOmics)

DIABLO finds latent components correlated **across** the omics blocks while
separating ripening stage, and selects a sparse set of features per block.

```{python}
#| echo: false
Markdown("**Block-to-block correlation (component 1 variates):** how strongly the "
         "blocks agree on the dominant axis of variation.")
```

# Part 2 — Reducing the large proteomics block

Proteomics (~5,000 features) dwarfs the other blocks (10s of features). Collapsing
it to a few factors **balances the blocks** and yields interpretable axes — this
is principled preprocessing, described, not an arbitrary modelling choice.

```{python}
#| echo: false
Markdown("**PCA variance explained** (proteomics):")
```

# Part 3 — Descriptive model panel (CV as a guardrail)

Each approach under leave-one-out CV. **This is not a leaderboard** — at n=9 a
single CV score is noisy; read it as "does this clear the majority baseline
(~33%) and not obviously overfit?", not as a precise ranking. For the ordered
target, MAE (ordinal distance) is the honest error.

```{python}
#| echo: false
res["panel"].round(3)
```

# Part 4 — How much to trust this

```{python}
#| echo: false
r = res["resolution"]
Markdown(
    f"- **n = {res['n_samples']}** — treat everything as **exploratory** and "
    f"cross-check methods/biology.\n"
    f"- **Easy structure:** the three ripening stages are strongly separated, so "
    f"most methods reach high accuracy — that means the *signal is clear*, not "
    f"that any one model is 'best'.\n"
    f"- **Resolution floor:** the smallest p-value this design can produce is "
    f"≈ {r['finest_two_sided_p']:.2g}; report effect size first.\n"
    f"- **Validated tools:** DIABLO = R mixOmics::block.splsda; reductions =\n"
    f"  PCA/NMF (sklearn). Data z-scored once; no double-scaling; NMF ran on\n"
    f"  non-negative log2 data.\n"
    f"- **Independent unit:** each banana is its own sample (assumed different\n"
    f"  fruit per stage, not one fruit tracked over time). If that assumption is\n"
    f"  wrong (same fruit), CV should group by fruit instead."
)
```

# Methods

Multi-omics integration via the reference R implementation (mixOmics DIABLO);
dimensionality reduction via PCA / NMF (sklearn); ordered classification via
ordinal regression (`mord`); Random Forest / sparse PLS-DA (sklearn / native).
All cross-validation is leave-one-out over independent samples; preprocessing is
missing-aware log + z-score (scaled once).
